title: X Feed Digest
summary: Anthropic dominated the batch: Project Glasswing and Claude Mythos Preview pushed frontier AI out of the usual benchmark discourse and into real cybersecurity and infrastructure risk management.
The coding-agent race is now clearly two-sided: closed products are scaling hard in usage, while open models like GLM-5.1 keep narrowing the capability gap on longer-horizon work.
Compute is increasingly an industrial story, not just a model story — posts from xAI and Intel pointed to a race defined by training scale, fabs, packaging, and power-hungry buildouts.
Outside AI, the cleanest market signals were geopolitical and supply-chain driven: Iran deadline risk, energy-cost pressure, and mineral dependence all remained live constraints beneath the tape.

items.title: @AnthropicAI: Glasswing Restricts Mythos
items.body: Anthropic unveiled Project Glasswing around Claude Mythos Preview, saying the model is powerful enough at vulnerability discovery that it will be limited to a small set of major infrastructure partners instead of released broadly. The real signal is that top-tier model progress is no longer just benchmark theater; labs are starting to treat some capability jumps as cyber-risk management problems.

items.title: @Zai_org: GLM-5.1 Raises the Open-Source Ceiling
items.body: Z.ai launched GLM-5.1 with claims of top open-source results on SWE-Bench Pro, Terminal-Bench, and NL2Repo plus up to eight-hour autonomous runs. Even if the numbers need independent vetting, the clear takeaway is that open agentic coding models are pushing into much longer-horizon tasks.

items.title: @sama: Codex Hits 3M Weekly Users
items.body: Sam Altman said Codex passed 3 million weekly users and that OpenAI is resetting usage limits at each additional million up to 10 million. That is a strong adoption signal for AI coding tools, and it suggests OpenAI is willing to spend compute aggressively to keep momentum high.

items.title: @ClaudeCodeLog: Claude Code Defaults Get More Serious
items.body: Claude Code 2.1.94 quietly moved default effort from medium to high for several paid setups and improved memory handling so MEMORY.md is no longer treated as empty. The practical takeaway is that wrapper behavior and defaults are still changing materially, so tool updates can alter results even when the underlying model name stays the same.

items.title: @elonmusk: Colossus 2 Training Lineup Expands
items.body: Musk said Colossus 2 now has seven models in training, including 1T, 1.5T, 6T, and 10T variants plus Imagine V2. Whether or not every name matters, the broader message is obvious: the frontier race is now being signaled through sheer training scale and parallel model bets.

items.title: @intel: Terafab Turns Compute Demand Into Factory Demand
items.body: Intel said it is joining the Terafab project alongside SpaceX, xAI, and Tesla to help build toward 1 TW/year of compute capacity. The investable read-through is that AI demand is still cascading down into fabs, packaging, and energy-hungry physical infrastructure.

items.title: @FactSet: Iran Deadline Keeps Event Risk Elevated
items.body: FactSet’s StreetAccount note said traders were watching whether Trump strikes a deal, delays, or escalates ahead of an Iran deadline, with uncertainty still high. For markets, it’s a reminder that geopolitics remains the fastest path to a fresh volatility spike even when underlying positioning looks steadier.

items.title: @kiteandkeymedia: Critical Minerals Still Underwrite the Whole Stack
items.body: Kite & Key’s video thread argued that American economic, military, and tech capacity all depend on imported minerals that are often controlled by geopolitical rivals. It’s a useful framing device for why supply-chain security remains a first-order constraint on everything from semis to defense.

items.title: @chenchengpro: A Hidden Tailscale DERP Trap in China
items.body: A concrete ops post: after self-hosting a Tailscale DERP relay in mainland China, the author found Alibaba Cloud will reset 80/443 traffic for domains without ICP filing even when localhost checks look fine. The useful trick is to move the relay off standard ports like 8443 if you want a no-surprises setup.

items.title: @PawelHuryn: Local Logs Can Expose Claude Code Spend
items.body: Pawel Huryn shared a dashboard that reads Claude Code’s local JSONL logs to break down sessions, tokens, and cache usage by project. The broader tip is simple: a lot of agent tooling already writes the telemetry you wish the UI exposed, so local introspection can recover it.

items.title: @dotey: LLM Wiki Beats More Bookmarks
items.body: Dotey’s thread argued that the real leap in personal knowledge tools is not raw collection but having an agent turn scattered clips into structured wiki pages you can actually revisit. That’s a good mental model for anyone drowning in bookmarks, highlights, and read-later debt.
